current.text: Detroit's projected starting five is Cunningham, Robinson, Thompson, Collins and Duren, so Holland comes off the bench. In the projected bench order he is second, behind sixth man Isaiah Joe and ahead of Paul Reed and Daniss Jenkins.
He is expected to share the floor with Ausar Thompson more this season instead of being staggered with him.
Detroit's power forward depth is very weak unless Thompson and Holland play the four, which could open frontcourt minutes for him.
Detroit ran a deep 12 to 13 player rotation last season that limited everyone's minutes.
Detroit is projected to win 50 to 51 games and finish third or fourth in the East.
Detroit plays 4-3-4 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21 and has 15 back-to-backs. No rest risk is expected.
Both sites rank him well outside the 144 players our league drafts, so he projects as a waiver player, not a draft target.

note: Neither site gives him any value (0 USD at both, rank 269 on Yahoo and 244 on ESPN), and he was not drafted in our league, so he should not be drafted in a 144-player auction. His appeal is steals for his minutes (1.2 in 19.8 minutes last season) and few turnovers. He has no flagged category, so he does not fit any specific build. Early in the season, check whether he gets power forward minutes next to Ausar Thompson and plays over 20 minutes a night, and whether his FT% holds near last season's 80.5% (Yahoo projects 68.2%).
